solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Convinced company's boss ran it badly

parts.note: CE stands for chief executive, the head of a company

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is sure the firm's chief executive mismanaged things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns RAN IT into ERTAIN, which follows CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being convinced of something is being sure of it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Attitudes support show finishing early on Monday in these conditions

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports the others sits beneath them, so this comes last
stopping before the end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a circus is a travelling show
stances are attitudes or positions taken

explanation.surface: A cryptic picture of a show ending early on a Monday because of stances people take.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'support' puts STANCES at the bottom, under CIRCU (the show cut short) and M; 'in these' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumstances are the conditions or state of affairs surrounding an event.

clue.text: Straying can come at a high price

definitions.meaning: wandering about without a fixed course

definitions.text: can come at a high price
definitions.meaning: using a mobile phone abroad on a foreign network is notoriously expensive

explanation.surface: Wandering off course may prove costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Roaming means wandering, and mobile roaming charges are famously steep for phone use abroad.

clue.text: Over in the Hebrides I rarely get up

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A Hebridean confesses to seldom getting out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to ESIRA inside Hebrides I rarely, and 'Over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to get up, from bed or a seat.

clue.text: Clever to conceal one's very inauspicious beginning at birth

indicators.note: concealing means holding the following letters inside the first word

parts.note: natty can mean clever or deft as well as smart
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the start of the word, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A clever person hides a very unlucky start in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' puts IVI (I, V and the first letter of inauspicious) inside NATTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nativity is a birth, especially that of Christ.

clue.text: Tough to make limit without fraud

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so the second word is removed

parts.note: to constrict is to restrict or limit
a con is a swindle or fraud

explanation.surface: It is hard to impose restrictions without cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict rules are tough or severe ones, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Assured of rescue in a storm

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so the letters of the word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is guaranteed a rescue during a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure and assured both mean certain or guaranteed.

clue.text: Unwilling to relaunch product at the borders with a new model

indicators.note: only the outer stretches of the two-word phrase are kept, its middle being thrown away

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: A firm is reluctant to relaunch a product at the frontier with a new version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the borders' keeps the edges of 'relaunch product', REL and UCT, giving RELUCT, then A, N and T follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reluctant is being unwilling or disinclined, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lots of policemen keep a promise

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the second piece is held inside the first

parts.note: cops is slang for policemen
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Many police officers honour a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful or abundant, so it stands for a great quantity.

clue.text: Extraordinary article is true to life

indicators.note: something out of the ordinary has its letters taken out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An exceptional newspaper piece is faithful to reality.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic depiction is lifelike, showing things as they really are.

clue.text: Sick person to fight off retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is written backwards in this across answer

parts.note: to repel an attack is to fight it off

explanation.surface: An invalid tries to fend off retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper suffers from leprosy, so is a sick person.

clue.text: Reply sent out: "Surrounded — left to die in a blaze of glory"

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next pieces
out signals that the words are put out of order

parts.note: to end is to die or finish

explanation.surface: A dramatic reply reports being besieged and left to perish gloriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges REPLY SENT into RESPENTLY, and 'Surrounded' puts L and END inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resplendently means with dazzling splendour, so gloriously.

clue.text: Make one's followers go back to get shaved

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in reverse
being shaved means losing a little at each edge, so both end letters go

parts.note: a retinue is a band of followers attending an important person

explanation.surface: An instruction to make somebody's supporters retreat and have a shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get shaved' trims RETINUE to ETINU, then 'go back' turns it round; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to join them together into a single whole.

clue.text: You French touring around Cairo unfortunately just can't get enough to eat

definitions.text: just can't get enough to eat

indicators.note: touring around a place means going right round it, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: vous is French for you

indicators.note: the city's letters fall out badly, ending up in a new order

explanation.surface: A French visitor going round Cairo can never get enough food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the city into RACIO; 'just' is a link softening the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A voracious eater has a huge appetite and can never be satisfied.

clue.text: Urban destination for older travellers shows sound judgment?

parts.note: Saga is a British company offering holidays for the over-fifties
a city is an urban place to travel to

explanation.surface: A city break for pensioners is a wise choice.
explanation.walkthrough: Saga is a British firm selling holidays and insurance to people over fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is wisdom or shrewdness, the ability to judge well.

clue.text: French town with six missing blocks alteration of summons

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in its path, so this piece goes inside the next

parts.note: an alteration is a change

indicators.note: missing means the Roman number is left out of the French word

parts.note: ville is the French word for town
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A town in France, short of six, obstructs a change to a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' strips the Roman six from the French word for town, and 'blocks' lodges what is left inside the alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: A challenge is a summons to fight or compete, as in a call to a duel.

clue.text: Girl in poem checks veil regularly

parts.note: to dam a flow is to check or hold it back

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one is used

explanation.surface: A young woman in verse inspects her veil often.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is a poetic or archaic word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Nasty pet flu is foreign

indicators.note: something foreign is strange, so these letters are made strange by rearranging them

explanation.surface: An unpleasant animal illness comes from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful behaviour is malicious and nasty, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wrong way to cut a fish

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: The incorrect method for slicing a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong way' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Wrong' is the definition and 'way' gives ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To go astray is to go wrong or off course.

clue.text: Could be a drama with the stormy weather

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare wrote a play with this one-word title, so a drama might bear the name
a violent storm with strong winds

explanation.surface: A play might feature a scene of foul weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, and The Tempest is Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Show contempt for media manipulation about organisation of workers at post office

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: spin is the slanted presentation of news to the media
TU is short for trade union

explanation.surface: Spin doctors scorn a union at the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit upon someone is a gesture of utter scorn, so to treat them with contempt.

clue.text: Go ahead with advertising chance finally to give up

parts.note: PR, public relations, is promotional work akin to advertising

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: to cede is to yield or give up

explanation.surface: Someone in advertising decides to quit after a last chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to come before, or go ahead of, something else.

clue.text: Women's group's sphere of influence is halved for good reason

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, so its possessive gives WI's

indicators.note: halved means the back half of the word is cut away, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: a domain is an area of control or influence

explanation.surface: A women's group's influence is cut in half, and with good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women; the 'is' before 'halved' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is sound sense, the faculty of reasoning well.

clue.text: Gripe makes politician flat on his back in bed

indicators.note: the politician's pieces go inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
MP is a Member of Parliament
lain is what one has done after lying flat

explanation.surface: A grievance arises when a politician is laid up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat on his back' gives LAIN, the past participle of lie, not a word meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is a grievance or gripe.

clue.text: Word of reassurance to boost her ego a bit

indicators.note: only a small part of the phrase is taken, the letters running across its words

explanation.surface: Something said to bolster a woman's confidence slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as 'there, there', it comforts someone who is upset.

clue.text: Time to do something about setter being taken for granted

indicators.note: the action word wraps around the setter

parts.note: to act is to do something
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: It is time to act about a setter who is being presumed upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside ACT; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood or implied without being stated, so assumed.

clue.text: Unrelenting sun starts to turn everyone red before noon

parts.note: S is short for sun, as in Sunday

indicators.note: the beginning letters of the following words are taken

parts.note: N for noon, as in clock abbreviations

explanation.surface: A merciless sun makes everyone go red before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A stern person is strict and unrelenting.

clue.text: Wanting infected individual treated

indicators.note: treating something works on it, so the letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: I is one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A patient who caught an infection needs care.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting in the sense of lacking or falling short, as deficient does.

clue.text: Burn gas without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the gas surrounds the letter

parts.note: steam is water in gaseous form
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Fuel burns freely with nothing holding it back.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is a Scottish word for a small stream; 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England a burn is a brook or small river.

clue.text: Animal found in empty laboratory as a matter of chance

indicators.note: the animal is placed inside the remaining shell
emptying the word leaves only its outermost letters

parts.note: an otter is an aquatic mammal

explanation.surface: Discovering a creature in a deserted lab is pure luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outer letters of laboratory, which 'found in' wraps round the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is decided by drawing lots, so its outcome is purely luck.
